newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mitsui to join S.African zinc study.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui to join S.African zinc study.

text.p: Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co Ltd and Mitsui and Co Ltd have joined a feasibility study into a proposed 220,000-tonnes-a-year zinc refinery in South Africa, Gencor Ltd said on Tuesday.

The Mitsui group is a 24.5 percent participant in the study and the group's involvement at this stage gives it an option to acquire an equivalent level of participation in the final refinery, Gencor said in a statement.

Gencor, in conjunction with the state-run Industrial Development Corp, has been investigating the feasibility of constructing a state-of-the-art zinc refinery in South Africa's Eastern Cape Province since March 1996.

Gencor said Mitsui would bring proven expertise in the fields of refining, zinc concentrate production and international product marketing which would complement the in-house Gencor/Billiton engineering and marketing skills.

The 1.7-billion-rand refinery, if it goes ahead, would produce special high grade zinc, using largely imported concentrates. The plant would have the capacity for expansion to some 400,000 tonnes a year, making it one of the largest in the world.
Gencor officials said last year they expected to make a decision on whether to proceed with the project in 1997, and production could start in late 1999.
Zinc concentrates could be sourced from various origins -- including Australia, Alaska and Peru -- while zinc produced is likely to be exported mainly to the Far East.
